name: Cyclon
long_description: Cyclon is rebuilding the phone around AI. Instead of opening apps and tapping through screens, you tell your phone what you want and it does it for you. With one touch, you can spin up AI agents to control your phone or handle tasks in the background. AI isn’t just inside an app - it’s the phone itself.
one_liner: a phone where AI is the interface

launches.title: Cyclon : the AI phone to replace your iPhone
launches.tagline: a phone that uses your apps for you and builds the ones you need.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re Adam and Thomas, the founders of Cyclon.

**We’re building an AI phone to replace your iPhone.** Tell it what you want, and it uses your apps for you, or builds the ones you need.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=no4BYVy3RmY>

**Why we're building this**

We spend hours on our phones doing things we could explain in one sentence.

“Find the latest contract, send it to Thomas, then call him.”

Today, that means opening Drive, finding the document, checking permissions, copying a link, switching to WhatsApp, and making the call yourself.

AI is becoming capable of doing this work. We’re building a phone that gives it the access and context to follow the task through.

**How it works**

Cyclon puts AI in the operating system, so it can work across the phone’s apps and notifications.

**It uses the same apps you do.** In the demo, I receive a notification asking me to send yesterday’s pictures. My phone has already done the work in the background: identifying Alex in my photos and gathering the right pictures. All I have to do is approve.

**It builds real apps.** Describe what you need—for example, an app to practice Spanish. Cyclon writes the code in a sandbox, tests it, and fixes issues before installing it on the phone. These are real apps you can open and use, and they can connect to APIs.

**It handles notifications.** Cyclon summarizes what matters and explains what it filters out. Tell it “Hide NordVPN notifications,” and it remembers that as a rule. When something needs a response, you can ask it to act directly.

Tasks can keep running in the background while you do something else.

**What we want this to become**

We believe a phone should adapt to its user: remember preferences, handle recurring tasks, and build software for needs that existing apps don't cover.

Just as the iPhone brought the internet and social networks into people's pockets, we want to bring the full power of AI to everyone. Instead of opening apps, people will just have to ask.

That's why we're developing our own hardware alongside the operating system. We want to be a phone company, own our product end to end, and control the entire experience. We believe that's only possible when you own both the hardware and software.

**We're not just adding AI to a smartphone. We're building a superphone around what AI makes possible.**

**Where we are today**

Our first limited batch is a **Pixel 8a with Cyclon preinstalled**, while we develop our own device.

We’re looking for early users who will put it through everyday tasks and tell us where it falls short.

**Why us**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125873&key=user_uploads/1322666/b2acc036-b5e7-4797-8696-a1366c0ffc7c)

Thomas worked on Android at Google. Adam studied electronics and miniaturized hardware at EPFL. Together, we won YC’s Call-My-Agent hackathon against 90+ teams.

We wanted a phone we could give the whole task to, so we started building it.

**Get one**

**Pre-order for $199: cyclon.ai/preorder**

Use it for a week and tell us what still makes you reach for your iPhone.

Know someone who’s been waiting for a phone like this? Send them our way: [contact@cyclon.ai](mailto:contact@cyclon.ai).
